cities.coverage_note: OVapi national NL GTFS feed, clipped to the Amsterdam metro area
VBB Berlin-Brandenburg GTFS feed, clipped to the Berlin metro area. Data: VBB Verkehrsverbund Berlin-Brandenburg GmbH (CC BY 4.0).

Milan's public transport: metro (M1-M5), trams and buses from ATM, plus Trenord suburban rail. The S-lines serving Milan are complete; Trenord's longer regional R/RE services are shown only where they run near the city. Walking ripples are drawn across the Milan urban area, so the most distant S-line stations appear as arrivals without a walk ripple. Data (c) Comune di Milano / AMAT - ATM (CC BY 3.0 IT) and (c) Trenord (CC BY 4.0).

MTA New York City Transit subway (regular schedule) and Staten Island Railway; Long Island Rail Road; Metro-North Railroad; NYCT local bus for all five boroughs (Bronx, Brooklyn, Manhattan, Queens, Staten Island); MTA Bus Company. Rail-outage shuttle buses (GTFS route_type 711) are folded into the bus mode alongside classic local buses; the Staten Island Railway (route_type 2, ships inside the subway feed) is shown as train, not metro. NOTE ON TIME WINDOW: the other cities animate a four-hour morning window (06:00-10:00); New York animates a shorter 90-minute morning-rush slice (06:00-07:30), anchored at the same 06:00 start, because the full federated nine-feed network exceeds the 25 MiB size budget over the longer window. No stops, routes, modes or feeds are dropped — every one of the nine MTA operators is fully represented; only the span of time SHOWN is shorter than the other cities'. Data: Metropolitan Transportation Authority, https://www.mta.info/developers.

Ruter's Oslo and Akershus GTFS feed, clipped to the Oslo metro area. T-bane, tram, bus and Oslofjord ferries. Data: Ruter, published via Entur (entur.org) under the Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD).

Toei network (Bureau of Transportation, Tokyo Metropolitan Government): the Asakusa, Mita, Shinjuku and Ōedo subway lines, the Tokyo Sakura Tram (Toden Arakawa Line), and the Nippori-Toneri Liner. Tokyo Metro and JR East (including the Yamanote Line) are NOT shown: their data licences prohibit public redistribution of a derived product, whereas Toei's feed is CC BY 4.0. Data: Bureau of Transportation, Tokyo Metropolitan Government, via the Public Transportation Open Data Center (odpt.org), CC BY 4.0.
Wiener Linien GTFS feed (Vienna city transit: U-Bahn, tram and bus). Data: Wiener Linien GmbH & Co KG via data.gv.at (CC BY 4.0).

Warsaw's ZTM public transport network: metro (M1, M2), trams, buses and SKM commuter rail. Data by Zarzad Transportu Miejskiego w Warszawie (ZTM), GTFS build by Mikolaj Kuranowski (mkuran.pl); bus route shapes from OpenStreetMap.

Swiss national GTFS timetable, clipped to the Zürich metro area. S-Bahn, tram, bus and lake boats; funiculars and aerial cableways are shown as rail. Data: Open data platform mobility Switzerland (opentransportdata.swiss), published by SBB on behalf of the Swiss Federal Office of Transport.
